tls proxy — Get the detail of generating certificate files
tls proxy — The implementation of SSL or TSL mutual authentication involves a client, a server, and a certificate authority (CA). A CA is used to ensure that the certificate between a client and a server is legal.
tls proxy — Tips: Run ```man openssl``` or see [the openssl manual page](https://www.openssl.org/docs/) for more information about using the OpenSSL command.
tls proxy — Generate an RSA private key for the ca.
tls proxy — Request to generate a CA certificate. You need to provide the basic information about the CA in this step. And you can get a ca.pem file , a CA certificate that can be used to generate client-server certificates. Choose the x509 option to skip the request and directly generate a self-signing certificate.
tls proxy — Generating a server certificate involves three steps and is similar to generating a client certificate.
tls proxy — Generate a server private key. You will get a ```server.key``` file.
tls proxy — Generate a certificate signing request file, and provide the required information about the server. After running the following command, you will get a ```server.csr``` file.
tls proxy — Open the ```server.csr```, the ```ca.key``` and the ```ca.pem``` files to sign the certificate. The ```CAcreateserial``` command option is used to create a CA serial number file if it does not exist. You will get ```aca.srl``` file after choosing this command option.
tls proxy — Modify Milvus Server config
tls proxy — Configure the file paths of `server.pem`, `server.key`, and `ca.pem` for the server in `config/milvus.yaml`.
tls proxy — One-way authentication
tls proxy — Server-side needs server.pem and server.key files, client-side needs server.pem file.
tls proxy — Two-way authentication
tls proxy — Server-side needs server.pem, server.key and ca.pem files, client-side needs client.pem, client.key and ca.pem files.

timetravel — Time Travel Implementation (Segment Level)
timetravel — Currently， there are two paths to implement time travel:
timetravel — Restrict with vec_count, used in growing segment.
timetravel — Generate bitmask and combine it with DSL calculation results. It is mainly used in the sealed segment.
timetravel — Growing Segment Time Travel
timetravel — When inserting, ensure that the inserted data is in ascending time order.
timetravel — Find the location of timestamp with binary search and record it as vec_count.
timetravel — Call vector_search interface and rest is handled inside segment, no need to handle bitmask generated by DSL.
timetravel — SealedSegment Time Travel
timetravel — During load, data is placed in a continuous memory area named chunk, with the following properties:
timetravel — Data is divided into multiple segments.
timetravel — Data in one segment is ordered by primary key.
timetravel — Data between Segments is in timestamp order. That is, the timestamp of every entity in the previous segment must be less than the timestamp of the first entity in the next segment.
timetravel — The Algorithm for time travel is:
timetravel — Use get_active_count interface, find the last segment containing a legal ts, and return the last element position of this segment as vec_count.
timetravel — Calculate the bitset mask with a timestamp. Due to the above properties, all the entities of the previous segment meet the conditions, and all the subsequent segments do not meet the conditions. Only the "last segment" needs to be calculated.
timetravel — the calculated results of Bitset and DSL are combined and sent to vector search interface.
segment sealed — SegmentSealed
segment sealed — SegmentSealed has an extra interface rather than SegmentInterface:
segment sealed — `LoadIndex(loadIndexInfo)`: load the index. indexInfo contains:
segment sealed — `FieldId`
segment sealed — `IndexParams`: index parameters in KV structure KV
segment sealed — `VecIndex`: vector index
segment sealed — `LoadFieldData(loadFieldDataInfo)`: load column data, could be either scalar column or vector column
segment sealed — Note: indexes and vector data for the same column may coexist. Indexes are prioritized in the search
segment sealed — `DropIndex(fieldId)`: drop and release an existing index of a specified field
segment sealed — Search is executable as long as all the columns involved in the search are loaded.
segment sealed — SegmentSealedImpl internal data definition
segment sealed — `row_count_opt_`:
segment sealed — Fill row count when loading the first entity
segment sealed — All the other columns loaded must match the same row count
segment sealed — `xxx_ready_bitset_` & `system_ready_count_`
segment sealed — Used to record whether the corresponding column is loaded. Bitset corresponds to FieldOffset
segment sealed — Query is executable if and only if all the following conditions are met:
segment sealed — system_ready_count_ == 2， which means all the system columns' RowId/Timestamp are loaded
segment sealed — The scalar columns involved in the query is loaded
segment sealed — For the vector columns involved in the query, either the original data or the index is loaded
segment sealed — `scalar_indexings_`: store scalar index
segment sealed — Use StructuredSortedIndex in Knowhere
segment sealed — `primary_key_index_`: store index for pk column
segment sealed — Use brand new ScalarIndexBase format
segment sealed — Note: The functions here may overlap with scalar indexes. It is recommended to replace scalar index with ScalarIndexBase**
segment sealed — `field_datas_`: store original data
segment sealed — `aligned_vector<char>` format guarantees `int/float` data are aligned
segment sealed — `SealedIndexingRecord vecindexs_`: store vector index
segment sealed — `row_ids_/timestamps_`: RowId/Timestamp data
segment sealed — `TimestampIndex`: Index for Timestamp column
segment sealed — `schema`: schema
segment sealed — SegmentSealedImpl internal function definition
segment sealed — Most functions are the implementation of the corresponding functions of the segment interface, which will not be repeated here.
segment sealed — `update_row_count`: Used to update the row_count field.
segment sealed — `mask_with_timestamps`: Use Timestamp column to update search bitmask, used to support Time Travel function.
segment growing — SegmentGrowing
segment growing — Growing segment has the following additional interfaces:
segment growing — `PreInsert(size) -> reservedOffset`: serial interface, which reserves space for future insertion and returns the `reservedOffset`.
segment growing — `Insert(reservedOffset, size, ...Data...)`: write `...Data...` into range `[reservedOffset, reservedOffset + size)`. This interface is allowed to be called concurrently.
segment growing — `...Data...` contains row_ids, timestamps two system attributes, and other columns
segment growing — data columns can be stored either row-based or column-based.
segment growing — `PreDelete & Delete(reservedOffset, row_ids, timestamps)` is a delete interface similar to insert interface.
segment growing — Growing segment stores data in the form of chunk. The number of rows in each chunk is restricted by configs.
segment growing — Rows per segment are controlled by parameters `size_per_Chunk ` config
segment growing — When inserting, first allocate enough space to ensure `total_size <= num_chunk * size_per_chunk`, and then convert data from row format to column format.
segment growing — During a search, each 'chunk' will be searched, and the search results will be saved as 'subquery result', then reduced into TopK.
segment growing — Growing Segment also implements small batch index for vectors. The parameters of small batch index are preset in `segcore config`
segment growing — When `metric type` is specified in the schema, the default parameters will build an index for each chunk to accelerate query
segment growing — SegmentGrowingImpl internal
segment growing — SegcoreConfig: contains parameters for Segcore，it has to be specified before create segment
segment growing — InsertRecord: inserted data put to here
segment growing — DeleteRecord: wait for delete implementation
segment growing — IndexingRecord: contains data with small index
segment growing — SealedIndexing: Record not used anymore
segment growing — SegcoreConfig
segment growing — Manage chunk_sizeand small index parameters
segment growing — `parse_from` can parse from yaml files（this function is not enabled by default）
segment growing — refer to `${milvus}/internal/core/unittest/test_utils/test_segcore.yaml`
segment growing — `default_config` offers default parameters
segment growing — InsertRecord
segment growing — Used to manage concurrent inserted data, including:
segment growing — `atomic<int64_t> reserved` reserved space calculation
segment growing — `AckResponder` calculate which segment to insert, returns current segment offset
segment growing — `ConcurrentVector` stores data columns, each column has one concurrent vector
segment growing — The following steps are executed when insert,
segment growing — Serially Execute `PreInsert(size) -> reserved_offset` to allocate memory space, the address of space is `[reserved_offset, reserved_offset + size)` is reserved
segment growing — Parallelly execute `Insert(reserved_offset, size, ...Data...)` interface，copy data into the above memory address
segment growing — First of all，for `ConcurrentVector` of each column, call `grow_to_at_least` to reserve space
segment growing — For each column data, call `set_data_raw` interface to put data into corresponding locations.
segment growing — After execution finished，call`AddSegment` of `AckResponder` ，mark the space `[reserved_offset, reserved_offset + size)` to already inserted
segment growing — ConcurrentVector
segment growing — This is a column data storage that can be inserted concurrently. It is composed of multi-data chunks.
segment growing — After`grow_to_at_least(size)` called, reserve space no less than `size`
segment growing — `set_data_raw(element_offset, source, element_count)` point source to continuous piece of data
segment growing — `get_span(chunk_id)` get the span of the corresponding chunk
segment overview — Segment Overview
segment overview — There are currently two types of Segments
segment overview — Growing segment, dynamic insert is allowed, but can not load index for fast retrieving
segment overview — Sealed segment, dynamic insert is disabled, loading vector index is supported
segment overview — Both Segment types share the same interface, based on `SegmentInterface`, External callers only need to care about the behavior of the following interface as function declarations and corresponding constructor:
segment overview — `SegmentInterface`
segment overview — `SegmentGrowing` & `CreateGrowingSegment`
segment overview — `SegmentSealed` & `CreateSealedSegment`
segment overview — Other internal functions are hidden as implementation details in the following classes:
segment overview — `SegmentInternalInterface`
segment overview — `SegmentGrowingImpl`
segment overview — `SegmentSealedImpl`
segment overview — In principle, the reusable code logic of growing / sealed is written into the 'SegmentInternalInterface' as far as possible. The different parts of the two classes contain more different parts
segment overview — See more details about segments at:
segment overview — [segment_interface.md](segment_interface.md)
segment overview — [segment_growing.md](segment_growing.md)
segment overview — [segment_sealed.md](segment_sealed.md)
segment interface — Segment Interface
segment interface — External Interface
segment interface — `get_row_count`: Get the number of entities in the segment
segment interface — `get_schema`: Get the corresponding collection schema in the segment
segment interface — `GetMemoryUsageInBytes`: Get memory usage of a segment
segment interface — `Search(plan, placeholderGroup, timestamp) -> QueryResult`: Perform search operations according to the plan containing search parameters and predicate conditions, and return search results. Ensure that the time of all search results is before the specified timestamp(MVCC)
segment interface — `FillTargetEntry(plan, &queryResult)`: Fill the missing column data for search results based on target columns in the plan
segment interface — See design details `${milvus_root}/internal/core/src/segcore/SegmentInterface.h`
segment interface — Basic Concepts：
segment interface — Segment: Data is sharded into segments based on written timestamp, and the sharding logic is controlled by data coordinator.
segment interface — Chunk: Further division of segment data, chunk is continuous data for each column
segment interface — There will be only one chunk in each sealed segment.
segment interface — In growing segment, chunks are currently divided by a fixed number of rows. With data ingestion, the number of chunks will increase
segment interface — Span: Similar to std::span, point to continuous data in memory
segment interface — SystemField: Extra field stores system info, currently including RowID and Timestamp field.
segment interface — SegOffset: The entity identifier in the segment
segment interface — SegmentInternalInterface internal functions
segment interface — `num_chunk()`: total chunk number
segment interface — `size_per_chunk()`: length of each chunk
segment interface — `get_active_count(Timestamp)`: entity count after filter by Timestamp
segment interface — `chunk_data(FieldOffset, chunk_id) -> Span<T>`: return continuous data for specified column and chunk
segment interface — `chunk_scalar_index(FieldOffset, chunk_id) -> const StructuredIndex<T>&`: return the inverted index of specified column and chunk
segment interface — `num_chunk_index`: the number of indexes (including scalars and vector indexes) that have been created:
segment interface — In growing segment, this value is the number of chunks for which the inverted index has been created. In these chunks, the index can be used to speed up the calculation.
segment interface — SealedSegment must be 1
segment interface — `debug()`: debug is used to print extra information while debugging
segment interface — `vector_search (vec_count, query..., timestamp, bitset, output)`: Search the vector column
segment interface — `vec_count`: specifies how many entities participated in the vector search calculation, the rest of the segments are filtered out because their timestamp is larger than specified timestamp. This function is mainly used in growing segment as multi version control(MVCC)
segment interface — `query...`: multiple variables jointly specify the parameters and search vector
segment interface — `timestamp`: timestamp is used for time traveling, filter out data with timestamp. Mainly for sealed segment
segment interface — `bitset`: calculated bit mask value as an output
segment interface — `output`: output QueryResult
segment interface — `bulk_subscript(FieldOffset|SystemField, seg_offsets..., output)`:
segment interface — given seg_offsets, calculate `results[i] = FieldData[seg_offsets[i]]`, for GetEntityByIds
segment interface — FieldData is defined by FieldOffset or SystemField
segment interface — `search_ids(IdArray, timestamp) -> pair<IdArray, SegOffsets>`:
segment interface — Find the corresponding segment offsets according to the primary key in an id array
segment interface — The returned order is not guaranteed, but the two returned fields must correspond to each other one by one.
segment interface — Entities without PKs will not be returned
segment interface — `check_search(Plan)`: check if the Plan is valid
segment interface — It mainly checks whether the columns used in the plan have been loaded
Search — Segcore Search Design
Search — init: 7.23.2021, by [FluorineDog](https://github.com/FluorineDog)
Search — update: 2.10.2022, by [zhuwenxing](https://github.com/zhuwenxing)
Search — Search now supports two modes: json DSL mode and Boolean Expr mode. We will talk about the latter one in detail because the former has been deprecated and is only used in tests.
Search — The execution mode of Boolean Expr works as follows:
Search — client packs search expr, topk, and query vector into proto and sends to Proxy node.
Search — Proxy Node unmarshals the proto, parses it to logical plan, makes a static check, and generates protobuf IR.
Search — Query Node unmarshals the plan, generates an executable plan AST, and queries in the segcore.
Search — See details of expression usage at [Boolean Expression Rules](https://milvus.io/docs/v2.0.0/boolean.md)
Search — Segcore Search Process
Search — After obtaining the AST, the execution engine uses the visitor mode to explain and executes the whole AST tree:
Search — Each node includes two steps, a mandatory vector search and an optional predicate.
Search — If Predicate exists, execute predicate expression stage to generate bitset as the vector search bitmask.
Search — If Predicate does not exist, the vector search bitmask will be empty.
Search — Bitmask will be used to mark filtered out / deleted entities in the vector execution engine.
Search — Currently, Milvus supports the following node on the AST, visitor mode is used to interpret and execute from top to bottom and generate the final bitmask.
Search — LogicalUnaryExpr: not expression
Search — LogicalBinaryExpr: and or expression
Search — TermExpr: in expression `A in [1, 2, 3]`
Search — CompareExpr: compare expression `A > 1` `B <= 1`
Search — TermExpr and CompareExpr are leaf nodes of execution.
visitor — Visitor Pattern
visitor — Visitor Pattern is used in segcore for parse and execute Execution Plan.
visitor — Inside `${internal/core}/src/query/PlanNode.h`, contains physical plan for vector search:
visitor — `FloatVectorANNS` FloatVector search execution node
visitor — `BinaryVectorANNS` BinaryVector search execution node
visitor — `${internal/core}/src/query/Expr.h` contains physical plan for scalar expression:
visitor — `TermExpr` support operation like `col in [1, 2, 3]`
visitor — `RangeExpr` support constant compare with data column like `a >= 5` `1 < b < 2`
visitor — `CompareExpr` support compare with different columns, like `a < b`
visitor — `LogicalBinaryExpr` support and/or
visitor — `LogicalUnaryExpr` support not
visitor — Currently, under `${internal/core/src/query}` directory, there are the following visitors:
visitor — `ExecPlanNodeVistor` physical plan executor only supports ANNS node for now
basic types — Glossary
basic types — `Collection`: Data table containing multiple Segments.
basic types — `Segment`: The memory structure of storing a piece of data which supports concurrent insertion, deletion, query, index loading, monitoring and statistics.
basic types — `Schema`: Definition of collection data format, including
basic types — `vector<FieldMeta>`: Order list of FieldMeta.
basic types — `isAutoId`: If set to True , the default primary field is `RowId` and it is auto-generated.
basic types — `primaryKey`: (When `isAutoId = False`) Specify primary key field.
basic types — `FieldMeta`: Field properties, including
basic types — `DataType`: Data type, including Int8...Int64, Float, Double, FloatVector, BinaryVector and String later.
basic types — `Dim`: (When dataType is vector) Type vector dimension.
basic types — `metric_type`: (When dataType is vector type, optional) The metric type corresponding to this vector is related to the small-batch index and can be empty.
basic types — `FieldName`: Column name.
basic types — `FieldId`: Unique number of the column.
basic types — (hidden) `FieldOffset`: Which is the subscript of `vector<Field>` in the schema. The internal calculation of segcore is basically based on field offset.
basic types — `Span`: Similar to STD::span. It supports vector type of data and can be implicitly converted to `SpanBase` for interface overwrite.

README — Integration test
README — This folder contains the integration test for Milvus components.
README — How it works
README — The Milvus integration test framework is a comprehensive testing solution that runs multiple Milvus components as separate processes to simulate a real deployment environment. It provides a `MiniClusterV3` that manages the lifecycle of core Milvus components including MixCoord, Proxy, DataNode, QueryNode and StreamingNode.
README — The framework allows developers to:
README — Start/stop a new milvus cluster
README — Start/stop individual Milvus components
README — Monitor component states and metadata through etcd
README — Execute end-to-end test scenarios
README — Execute the method of any component from its client
README — Simulate component failures and recovery
README — Modify the milvus configration at runtime or startup
README — The test framework is built on top of Go's testing package and the testify/suite framework, making it easy to write structured and maintainable integration tests.
README — How to run integration test locally
README — Because integration test is a multi-process framework, it requires some components to start:
README — a built milvus binary
README — Build the milvus binary first.
README — Run the docker compose to start the etcd, minio and pulsar.
README — Run the integration test.
README — If you want to run single test case, you could execute command like this example
README — Recommended coding style for add new cases
README — Should I add a new test case into integration?
README — It's a good choice to add a new test case into integration test if:
README — The test case need to control the lifecycle of Milvus components, such as starting/stopping components or modifying configuration then executing some end-to-end scenarios.
README — If the test case is hard to apply in the unit-test and E2E test, such as testing in a non-default configured Milvus cluster, and need to be tested between multiple components.
README — Should not add a new test case into integration test if:
README — Function-verification that can be covered by unit test or already be covered by E2E test.
README — Performance test.
README — Using `suite`
README — MiniCluster` and `MiniClusterSuite` provides lots of comment preset tool function to execute intergration test.
README — It is recommend to add a new test with `testify/suite`
README — A suite will start a new empty milvus cluster, and the cluster will be reused for all test cases in the suite. We recommend to add more useful utility methods into `MiniClusterSuite` or `MilvusClusterV3` to interact with the cluster, to speed up the integration test development.
README — Some utility methods are provided in `MiniClusterSuite` to interact with the cluster:
README — method of `MiniClusterSuite`
README — Use `s.WithMilvusConfig` to modify the milvus configuration at startup in `SetupSuite` method.
README — Use `s.WithOptions` to modify the test options at startup in `SetupSuite` method.
README — Use `s.Cluster` to get the `MiniClusterV3` instance, which provides methods to interact with the Milvus cluster.
README — Some useful milvus method is provided in `util_` files, such as `CreateCollection`, `Insert`, `Flush`...,
README — method of `MiniClusterV3`
README — Use `s.Cluster.MustModifyMilvusConfig` to modify the milvus configuration at runtime, it will return a guard function to restore the modified configuration. It doesn't promise that the configuration will be applied immediately, milvus may not support the dynamic configuration change for some configurations or some configration may be applied slowly.
README — Use `s.Cluster.Add*` to add components to the cluster, such as `AddMixCoord`, `AddProxy`, `AddDataNode`, `AddQueryNode`, `AddStreamingNode`. it will return the `MilvusProcess` object to manage the lifetime of new incoming component. It will block until the component is healthy by default, use `WithoutWaitForReady` option to avoid it.
README — Use `s.Cluster.Default*` to get the default component, such as `DefaultMixCoord`, `DefaultProxy`, `DefaultDataNode`, `DefaultQueryNode`, `DefaultStreamingNode`.
README — Use `s.*Client` to get the grpc client of the default component that can be got from `s.Cluster.Default*`, such as `s.MixCoordClient`, `s.ProxyClient`, `s.DataNodeClient`, `s.QueryNodeClient`, `s.StreamingNodeClient`.
README — Use `s.MilvusClient` to get the grpc client of the Milvus server, which is connnected to the proxy that is returned from `DefaultProxy()`.
README — method of `MilvusProcess`
README — Use `p.MustGetClient` to get the grpc client of the component, which provides methods to interact with the component.
README — Use `p.MustWaitForReady` to wait for the component to be ready, it will block until the component is healthy.
README — Use `p.Stop` to stop the component, it will block until the component is stopped. It will perform a graceful shutdown by default. When the given deadline is excceed, `ForceStop` is performed.
README — Use `p.ForceStop` to force stop the component, it will not wait for the component to be stopped.
README — Use `p.IsWorking` to check if the component is working, it will return false if the component is stopped.
README — New folder for each new scenario
README — It's a known issue that integration test cases run in same process might affect due to some singleton component not fully cleaned.
README — As a temp solution, test cases are separated into different packages to run independently.
README — Some tips
README — Sometimes, if the test case is killed by some SIGKILL, it will leave some orphan milvus process running in the background. You could use `killall milvus` to kill all milvus process, or `killall -9 milvus` to kill all milvus process forcefully.
README — Because the test framework use some determined port (such as 53100 for coord, 19530 for proxy), it will be failed to start a new milvus process if the port is already in use. You could use `lsof -i :53100` to check if the port is already in use.
README — The test coverage of milvus can not be generated by the integration test, because that the integration test use multi-process. the test coverage only cover the code that is executed by the integration test itself.

README — Overview of the benchmark
README — Components
README — `main.py`
README — The entry file: parse the input params and initialize the other components: `metric`, `env`, `runner`
README — `metric`
README — The test result can be used to analyze the regression or improvement of the milvus system, so we upload the metrics of the test result when a test suite run finished, and then use `redash` to make sense of our data
README — Currently we use the `mongodb` to store the test result
README — The `env` component defines the server environment and environment management, the instance of the `env` corresponds to the run mode of the benchmark
README — `local`: Only defines the host and port for testing
README — `helm/docker`: Install and uninstall the server in benchmark stage
README — `runner`
README — The actual executor in benchmark, each test type defined in test suite will generate the corresponding runner instance, there are three stages in `runner`:
README — `extract_cases`: There are several test cases defined in each test suite yaml, and each case shares the same server environment and shares the same `prepare` stage, but the `metric` for each case is different, so we need to extract cases from the test suite before the cases runs
README — `prepare`: Prepare the data and operations, for example, before running searching, index needs to be created and data needs to be loaded
README — `run_case`: Do the core operation and set `metric` value
README — `suites`: There are two ways to take the content to be tested as input parameters：
README — Test suite files under `suites` directory
README — Test suite configmap name including `server_config_map` and `client_config_map` if using argo workflow
README — `update.py`: While using argo workflow as benchmark pipeline, we have two steps in workflow template: `install-milvus` and `client-test`

README CN — 工作目录及文件介绍
README CN — base**：放置已封装好的 **PyMilvus 模块文件**，以及 Pytest 框架的 setup 和 teardown 处理等
README CN — check**：接口返回结果的**检查模块**
README CN — common**：测试用例**通用的方法和参数**
README CN — config**：**基础配置**内容
README CN — testcases**：存放**测试用例**脚本
README CN — utils**：**通用程序**，如可用于全局的日志类、或者环境检查的方法等
README CN — requirements**：执行测试文件所**依赖**的 python 包
README CN — conftest.py**：编写**装饰器函数**，或者自己实现的**本地插件**，作用范围为该文件存放的目录及其子目录
README CN — pytest.ini**：pytest 的主**配置**文件
README CN — base/\*_warpper.py**: **封装被测接口**，统一处理接口请求，提取接口请求的返回结果，传入 **check/func_check.py** 模块进行结果检查。
README CN — check/func_check.py**: 模块编写各接口返回结果的检查方法，供测试用例调用。
README CN — base/client_base.py**: 模块使用pytest框架，进行相应的setup/teardown方法处理。
README CN — testcases** 目录下的测试文件，继承 **base/client_base.py** 里的 **TestcaseBase** 模块，进行相应的测试用例编写。用例里用到的通用参数和数据处理方法，写入**common**模块供用例调用。
README CN — config** 目录下加入一些全局配置，如日志的路径。
README CN — utils** 目录下负责实现全局的方法，如全局可用的日志模块。
README CN — 可参考添加新的测试用例或框架工具。
README CN — Python 测试代码添加注意事项
README CN — test 文件：每一个 SDK 类对应一个 test 文件，Load 和 Search 单独对应一个 test 文件
README CN — test类：每一个 test 文件中分两个类
README CN — TestObjectParams ：
README CN — 如 TestPartitionParams 表示 Partition Interface 参数检查测试用例类
README CN — 检查在不同输入参数条件下，目标类/方法的表现，参数注意覆盖default，empty，none，datatype，maxsize边界值等
README CN — TestObjectOperations:
README CN — 如 TestPartitionOperations 表示 Partition Interface 针对不同 function 或操作的测试
README CN — 检查在合法输入参数，与其他接口有一定交互的条件下，目标类/方法的返回和表现
README CN — testcase 命名
README CN — TestObjectParams 类
README CN — 以testcase输入参数区分命名，如 test_partition_empty_name() 表示验证空字符串作为 name 参数输入的表现
README CN — TestObjectOperations 类
README CN — 以 testcase 操作步骤区分命名，如 test_partition_drop_partition_twice() 表示验证连续 drop 两次 partition 的表现
README CN — 以 testcase 验证点区分命名，如 test_partition_maximum_partitions() 表示验证创建 partition 的最大数量
README CN — 不能在测试用例文件中初始化 PyMilvus 对象
README CN — 一般情况下，不在测试用例文件中直接添加日志代码

README — Working directories and files
README — base**: stores the encapsulated **PyMilvus** **module** files, and setup & teardown functions for pytest framework.
README — check**: stores the **check module** files for returned results from interface.
README — common**: stores the files of **common methods and parameters** for test cases.
README — config**: stores the **basic configuration file.**
README — testcases**: stores **test case scripts.**
README — utils**: stores **utility programs**, such as utility log and environment detection methods.
README — requirements.txt**: specifies the **python package** required for executing test cases
README — conftest.py**: you can compile fixture functions or local plugins in this file. These functions and plugins implement within the current folder and its subfolder.
README — pytest.ini**: the main configuration file for pytest.
README — Critical design ideas
README — base/\*_wrapper.py** encapsulates the tested interface, uniformly processes requests from the interface, abstracts the returned results, and passes the results to **check/func_check.py** module for checking.
README — check/func_check.py** encompasses result checking methods for each interface for invocation from test cases.
README — base/client_base.py** uses pytest framework to process setup/teardown functions correspondingly.
README — Test case files in **testcases** folder should be compiled inheriting the **TestcaseBase** module from **base/client_base.py**. Compile the common methods and parameters used by test cases into the **Common** module for invocation.
README — Add global configurations under **config** directory, such as log path, etc.
README — Add global implementation methods under **utils** directory, such as utility log module.
README — Adding codes
README — This section specifies references while adding new test cases or framework tools.
README — Notice and best practices
README — Coding style
README — Test files: each SDK category corresponds to a test file. So do `load` and `search` methods.
README — Test categories: test files fall into two categories
README — `TestObjectParams`:
README — Indicates the parameter test of corresponding interface. For instance, `TestPartitionParams` represents the parameter test for Partition interface.
README — Tests the target category/method under different parameter inputs. The parameter test will cover `default`, `empty`, `none`, `datatype`, `maxsize`, etc.
README — `TestObjectOperations`:
README — Indicates the function/operation test of corresponding interface. For instance, `TestPartitionOperations` represents the function/operation test for Partition interface.
README — Tests the target category/method with legit parameter inputs and interaction with other interfaces.
README — Testcase naming
README — Name after the parameter input of the test case. For instance, `test_partition_empty_name()` represents test on performance with the empty string as the `name` parameter input.
README — `TestObjectOperations`
README — Name after the operation procedure of the test case. For instance, `test_partition_drop_partition_twice()` represents the test on the performance when dropping partitions twice consecutively.
README — Name after assertions. For instance, `test_partition_maximum_partitions()` represents test on the maximum number of partitions that can be created.
README — Do not initialize PyMilvus objects in the test case files.
README — Generally, do not add log IDs to test case files.
README — Directly call the encapsulated methods or attributes in test cases, as shown below:
README — To create multiple partitions objects, call `self.init_partition_wrap()`, which returns the newly created partition objects. Call `self.partition_wrap` instead when you do not need multiple objects.
README — To test on the error or exception returned from interfaces:
README — Call `check_task=CheckTasks.err_res`.
README — Input the expected error ID and message.
README — To test on the normal value returned from interfaces:
README — Call `check_task=CheckTasks.check_partition_property`. You can build new test methods in `CheckTasks` for invocation in test cases.
README — Input the expected result for test methods.
README — Adding test cases
README — Find the encapsulated tested interface with the same name in the ***_wrapper.py** files under **base** directory. Each interface returns a list with two values, among which one is interface returned results of PyMilvus, and the other is the assertion of normal/abnormal results, i.e. `True`/`False`. The returned judgment can be used in the extra result checking of test cases.
README — Add the test cases in the corresponding test file of the tested interface in **testcases** folder. You can refer to all test files under this directory to create your own test cases as shown below:
README — Case comments encompass three parts: object, test method, and expected result. You should specify each part.
README — Initialize the tested category in the setup method of the Base category in the **base/client_base.py** file, as shown below:
README — Pass the parameters with corresponding encapsulated methods when calling the interface you need to test on. As shown below, align all parameters with those in PyMilvus interfaces except for `check_task` and `check_items`.
README — `check_task` is used to select the corresponding interface test method in the ResponseChecker check category in the **check/func_check.py** file. You can choose methods under the `CheckTasks` category in the **common/common_type.py** file.
README — The specific content of `check_items` passed to the test method is determined by the implemented test method `check_task`.
README — The tested interface can return normal results when `CheckTasks` and `check_items` are not passed.

README — Chaos Tests
README — Chaos tests are designed to check the reliability of Milvus.
README — For instance, if one pod is killed:
README — verify that it restarts automatically
README — verify that the related operation fails, while the other operations keep working successfully during the absence of the pod
README — verify that all the operations work successfully after the pod back to running state
README — verify that no data lost
README — Chaos tests run in pytest framework, same as e2e tests.
README — Please refer to [Run E2E Tests](https://github.com/milvus-io/milvus/blob/master/tests/README.md)
README — Flow Chart
README — <img src="../graphs/chaos_test_flow_chart.jpg" alt="Chaos Test Flow Chart" width=50%/>
README — pod kill
README — Kill pod every 5s
README — pod network partition
README — Two direction(to and from) network isolation between a pod and the rest of the pods
README — pod failure
README — Set the pod（querynode, indexnode and datanode）as multiple replicas, make one of them failure, and test milvus's functionality
README — pod memory stress
README — Limit the memory resource of pod and generate plenty of stresses over a group of pods
README — Milvus in standalone mode
README — standalone pod is killed
README — minio pod is killed
README — Test scenarios are designed by different chaos objects
README — Every chaos object is defined in one yaml file locates in folder `chaos_objects`
README — Every chaos yaml file specified by `ALL_CHAOS_YAMLS` in `constants.py` would be parsed as a parameter and be passed into `test_chaos.py`
README — All expectations of every scenario are defined in `testcases.yaml` locates in folder `chaos_objects`
README — [Chaos Mesh](https://chaos-mesh.org/) is used to inject chaos into Milvus in `test_chaos.py`
README — Run a single test scenario manually(take query node pod is killed as instance):
README — update `ALL_CHAOS_YAMLS = 'chaos_querynode_podkill.yaml'` in `constants.py`
README — Run multiple test scenario in a category manually(take network partition chaos for all pods as instance):
README — update `ALL_CHAOS_YAMLS = 'chaos_*_network_partition.yaml'` in `constants.py`
README — Automation Scripts
README — Run test scenario automatically:
README — update chaos type and pod in `chaos_test.sh`

README — How to contribute
README — Get familiar with chaos engineering and [Chaos Mesh](https://chaos-mesh.org)
README — Design chaos scenarios, preferring to pick from todo list
README — Generate yaml file for your chaos scenarios. You can create a chaos experiment in chaos-dashboard, then download the yaml file of it.
README — Add yaml file to chaos_objects dir and rename it as `chaos_${component_name}_${chaos_type}.yaml`. Make sure `kubectl apply -f ${your_chaos_yaml_file}` can take effect
README — Add testcase in `testcases.yaml`. You should figure out the expectation of milvus during the chaos
README — Run your added testcase according to `Manually` above and check whether it as your expectation

README — Index Type Support
README — Scalar Index Types
README — | Data Types | INVERTED | BITMAP | STL_SORT | Trie | NGRAM | AUTOINDEX |
README — |:---------------------------------------------------------|:--------:|:------:|:--------:|:----:|:-----:|:---------:|
README — | INT8, INT16, INT32, INT64 | yes | yes | yes | no | no | yes |
README — | BOOL | yes | yes | no | no | no | yes |
README — | FLOAT, DOUBLE | yes | no | yes | no | no | yes |
README — | VARCHAR | yes | yes | no | yes | yes | yes |
README — | JSON | yes | no | no | no | yes* | yes |
README — | ARRAY (elements: BOOL, INT8, INT16, INT32, INT64, VARCHAR) | yes | yes | no | no | no | yes |
README — | ARRAY (elements: FLOAT, DOUBLE) | yes | no | no | no | no | yes |
README — JSON fields require `json_path` and `json_cast_type: "varchar"` parameters for NGRAM index
README — NGRAM Index Specific Features
README — The NGRAM index is specialized for efficient text partial matching and fuzzy search on VARCHAR and JSON fields.
README — Supported Fields:**
README — VARCHAR**: Direct text content indexing
README — JSON**: Requires `json_path` parameter to specify the JSON field path (e.g., `field_name['key']`)
README — Index Parameters:**
README — `min_gram`: Minimum n-gram length (required, positive integer)
README — `max_gram`: Maximum n-gram length (required, positive integer, ≥ min_gram)
README — `json_path`: JSON field path for JSON fields (e.g., `"json_field['body']"`)
README — `json_cast_type`: Must be `"varchar"` for JSON fields
README — Performance Characteristics:**
README — Optimized for LIKE queries with `%` and `_` wildcards
README — Two-phase query execution: n-gram filtering + secondary validation
README — Query strings shorter than `min_gram` fall back to full table scan
README — Supports multilingual text including Chinese, Japanese, and Korean
README — Example Index Creation:**

README — Graceful handling of unsupported expressions

README — Result count and ID verification
README — Index consistency verification
README — LIKE Pattern Coverage
README — Prefix patterns: `str%`
README — Suffix patterns: `%str`
README — Contains patterns: `%str%`
README — Single character wildcard: `str_`, `_str`
README — Combination patterns: `str_%`, `%_str`
README — Escape patterns: `str\%`, `str\_`
README — NGRAM Index Optimization:**
README — LIKE queries on VARCHAR and JSON fields with NGRAM index are automatically optimized
README — Query performance significantly improves for pattern matching operations
README — Supports all LIKE patterns with `%` and `_` wildcards
README — Automatic fallback to full scan when query length < `min_gram`

README — Data Node
README — DataNode is the component to write insert and delete messages into persistent blob storage, for example MinIO or S3.
README — Dependency
README — KV store: a kv store that persists messages into blob storage.
README — Message stream: receive messages and publish information
README — Root Coordinator: get the latest unique IDs.
README — Data Coordinator: get the flush information and which message stream to subscribe.
README — Data Coordinator
README — Data cooridnator(datacoord for short) is the component to organize DataNodes and segments allocations.
README — KV store: a kv store has all the meta info datacoord needs to operate. (etcd)
README — Message stream: a message stream to communicate statistics information with data nodes. (Pulsar)
README — Root Coordinator: timestamp, id and meta source.
README — Data Node(s): could be an instance or a cluster, actual worker group handles data modification operations.
README — Generate Parser with Antlr4
README — Install Antlr4
README — Please follow [install antlr4](https://github.com/antlr/antlr4/blob/master/doc/go-target.md) to install the antlr tool.
README — The version of antlr tool: `4.13.2`.
README — Code Generate
README — After you install the antlr4, you can generate the parser code in golang with:
README — All generated code will be under directory `generated`.
README — Session Package
README — `session` package contains the worker manager/nodes abstraction for datanodes and indexnodes.
README — pkoracle package
README — This package defines the interface and implementations for segments bloom filter sets of flushcommon metacache.
README — BloomFilterSet
README — The basic implementation with segment statslog. A group of bloom filter to perdict whethe some pks exists in the segment.
README — LazyPkStats
README — A wrapper for lazy loading PkStats. The inner PkStats could be added async.
README — CANNOT* be used for growing segment.
README — `wal` package is the basic defination of wal interface of milvus streamingnode.
README — `wal` use `github.com/milvus-io/milvus/pkg/streaming/walimpls` to implement the final wal service.
README — Project arrangement
README — `/`: only define exposed interfaces.
README — `/adaptor/`: adaptors to implement `wal` interface from `walimpls` interface
README — `/utility/`: A utility code for common logic or data structure.
README — `github.com/milvus-io/milvus/pkg/streaming/walimpls`
README — `/`: define the underlying message system interfaces need to be implemented.
README — `/registry/`: A static lifetime registry to regsiter new implementation for inverting dependency.
README — `/helper/`: A utility used to help developer to implement `walimpls` conveniently.
README — `/impls/`: A official implemented walimpls sets.
README — Lifetime Of Interfaces
README — `OpenerBuilder` has a static lifetime in a programs:
README — `Opener` keep same lifetime with underlying resources (such as mq client).
README — `WAL` keep same lifetime with underlying writer of wal, and it's lifetime is always included in related `Opener`.
README — `Scanner` keep same lifetime with underlying reader of wal, and it's lifetime is always included in related `WAL`.
README — Add New Implemetation Of WAL
README — developper who want to add a new implementation of `wal` should implements the `github.com/milvus-io/milvus/pkg/streaming/walimpls` package interfaces. following interfaces is required:
README — `walimpls.OpenerBuilderImpls`
README — `walimpls.OpenerImpls`
README — `walimpls.ScannerImpls`
README — `walimpls.WALImpls`
README — `OpenerBuilderImpls` create `OpenerImpls`; `OpenerImpls` creates `WALImpls`; `WALImpls` create `ScannerImpls`.
README — Then register the implmentation of `walimpls.OpenerBuilderImpls` into `github.com/milvus-io/milvus/pkg/streaming/walimpls/registry` package.
README — All things have been done.
README — package `adaptor` is used to adapt `walimpls` and `wal` together.
README — common wal function should be implement by it. Such as:
README — lifetime management
README — interceptor implementation
README — scanner wrapped up
README — write ahead cache implementation

README — [![Build Status](https://travis-ci.org/joboccara/NamedType.svg?branch=master)](https://travis-ci.org/joboccara/NamedType)
README — ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/github/license/joboccara/pipes)
README — A **strong type** is a type used in place of another type to carry specific **meaning** through its **name**.
README — This project experiments with strong types in C++. All components are in the namespace `fluent`. You can find a collection of blog posts explaining the rationale of the library and usages for strong types on [Fluent C++](https://www.fluentcpp.com/2016/12/08/strong-types-for-strong-interfaces/).
README — <a href="https://www.patreon.com/join/fluentcpp?"><img alt="become a patron" src="https://c5.patreon.com/external/logo/become_a_patron_button.png" height="35px"></a>
README — Basic usage
README — It central piece is the templated class NamedType, which can be used to declare a strong type with a typedef-like syntax:
README — which can be used to make interfaces more expressive and more robust.
README — Note how the below constructor shows in which order it expects its parameters:
README — Strong types are about better expressing your intentions, both to the compiler and to other human developers.**
README — Strong typing over generic types
README — This implementation of strong types can be used to add strong typing over generic or unknown types such as lambdas:
README — Strong typing over references
README — The NamedType class is designed so that the following usage:
README — behaves like a reference on an std::string, strongly typed.
README — Inheriting the underlying type functionalities
README — You can declare which functionalities should be inherited from the underlying type. So far, only basic operators are taken into account.
README — For instance, to inherit from operator+ and operator<<, you can declare the strong type:
README — There is one special skill, `FunctionCallable`, that lets the strong type be converted in the underlying type. This has the effect of removing the need to call .get() to get the underlying value. And `MethodCallable` enables `operator->` on the strong type to invoke methods on the underlying type.
README — The skill `Callable` is the union of `FunctionCallable` and `MethodCallable`.
README — Named arguments
README — By their nature strong types can play the role of named parameters:
README — But the nested type `argument` allows to emulate a named argument syntax:
README — You can have a look at tests.cpp for usage examples.

country211 — The Country211 Dataset
country211 — In the paper, we used an image classification dataset called Country211, to evaluate the model's capability on geolocation. To do so, we filtered the YFCC100m dataset that have GPS coordinate corresponding to a [ISO-3166 country code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_3166_country_codes) and created a balanced dataset by sampling 150 train images, 50 validation images, and 100 test images images for each country.
country211 — The following command will download an 11GB archive countaining the images and extract into a subdirectory `country211`:
country211 — These images are a subset of the YFCC100m dataset. Use of the underlying media files is subject to the Creative Commons licenses chosen by their creators/uploaders. For more information about the YFCC100M dataset, visit [the official website](https://multimediacommons.wordpress.com/yfcc100m-core-dataset/).
yfcc100m — The YFCC100M Subset
yfcc100m — In the paper, we performed a dataset ablation using a subset of the YFCC100M dataset and showed that the performance remained largely similar.
yfcc100m — The subset contains 14,829,396 images, about 15% of the full dataset, which have been filtered to only keep those with natural languag titles and/or descriptions in English.
yfcc100m — We provide the list of (line number, photo identifier, photo hash) of each image contained in this subset. These correspond to the first three columns in the dataset's metadata TSV file.
yfcc100m — Use of the underlying media files is subject to the Creative Commons licenses chosen by their creators/uploaders. For more information about the YFCC100M dataset, visit [the official website](https://multimediacommons.wordpress.com/yfcc100m-core-dataset/).
prompts — Prompts for Image Classification
prompts — Below are the class names and templates that are used for collecting the zero-shot classification scores in the paper. Each dataset has two lists `classes` and `templates`, where the string `{}` in the template is to be replaced with the corresponding class names. For the Facial Emotion Recognition 2013 dataset specifically, we used multiple class names for certain classes.
prompts — This file contains prompt data for 26 of the 27 datasets shown in Table 9 of the paper; the text prompts for ImageNet (as well as other [ImageNet Testbed](https://modestyachts.github.io/imagenet-testbed/) datasets in Figure 13) can be found in [this notebook](https://github.com/openai/CLIP/blob/main/notebooks/Prompt_Engineering_for_ImageNet.ipynb), as well as how to ensemble predictions from multiple prompts using these templates.

README — Dockers for `transformers`
README — In this folder you will find various docker files, and some subfolders.
README — dockerfiles (ex: `consistency.dockerfile`) present under `~/docker` are used for our "fast" CIs. You should be able to use them for tasks that only need CPU. For example `torch-light` is a very light weights container (703MiB).
README — subfolders contain dockerfiles used for our `slow` CIs, which *can* be used for GPU tasks, but they are **BIG** as they were not specifically designed for a single model / single task. Thus the `~/docker/transformers-pytorch-gpu` includes additional dependencies to allow us to run ALL model tests (say `librosa` or `tesseract`, which you do not need to run LLMs)
README — Note that in both case, you need to run `uv pip install -e .`, which should take around 5 seconds. We do it outside the dockerfile for the need of our CI: we checkout a new branch each time, and the `transformers` code is thus updated.
README — We are open to contribution, and invite the community to create dockerfiles with potential arguments that properly choose extras depending on the model's dependencies! :hugs:
TRANSLATING — Translating the Transformers documentation into your language
TRANSLATING — As part of our mission to democratize machine learning, we aim to make the Transformers library available in many more languages! Follow the steps below to help translate the documentation into your language.
TRANSLATING — Open an Issue
TRANSLATING — Navigate to the Issues page of this repository.
TRANSLATING — Check if anyone has already opened an issue for your language.
TRANSLATING — If not, create a new issue by selecting the "Translation template" from the "New issue" button.
TRANSLATING — Post a comment indicating which chapters you’d like to work on, and we’ll add your name to the list.
TRANSLATING — Fork the Repository
TRANSLATING — First, fork the Transformers repo by clicking the Fork button in the top-right corner.
TRANSLATING — Clone your fork to your local machine for editing with the following command:
TRANSLATING — Replace `YOUR-USERNAME` with your GitHub username.
TRANSLATING — Copy-paste the English version with a new language code
TRANSLATING — The documentation files are organized in the following directory:
TRANSLATING — docs/source**: This contains all documentation materials organized by language.
TRANSLATING — To copy the English version to your new language directory:
TRANSLATING — Navigate to your fork of the repository:
TRANSLATING — Replace `~/path/to` with your actual path.
TRANSLATING — Run the following command:
TRANSLATING — Replace `LANG-ID` with the appropriate ISO 639-1 or ISO 639-2 language code (see [this table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes) for reference).
TRANSLATING — Start translating
TRANSLATING — Begin translating the text!
TRANSLATING — Start with the `_toctree.yml` file that corresponds to your documentation chapter. This file is essential for rendering the table of contents on the website.
TRANSLATING — If the `_toctree.yml` file doesn’t exist for your language, create one by copying the English version and removing unrelated sections.
TRANSLATING — Ensure it is placed in the `docs/source/LANG-ID/` directory.
TRANSLATING — Here’s an example structure for the `_toctree.yml` file:
TRANSLATING — Once you’ve translated the `_toctree.yml`, move on to translating the associated MDX files.
TRANSLATING — Collaborate and share
TRANSLATING — If you'd like assistance with your translation, open an issue and tag `@stevhliu`. Feel free to share resources or glossaries to ensure consistent terminology.

README — Renaming section headers and moving sections
README — It helps to keep the old links working when renaming the section header and/or moving sections from one document to another. This is because the old links are likely to be used in Issues, Forums, and Social media and it'd make for a much more superior user experience if users reading those months later could still easily navigate to the originally intended information.
README — Therefore, we simply keep a little map of moved sections at the end of the document where the original section was. The key is to preserve the original anchor.
README — So if you renamed a section from: "Section A" to "Section B", then you can add at the end of the file:
README — and of course, if you moved it to another file, then:
README — Use the relative style to link to the new file so that the versioned docs continue to work.
README — For an example of a rich moved section set please see the very end of [the Trainer doc](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/docs/source/en/main_classes/trainer.md).
README — Writing Documentation - Specification
README — The `huggingface/transformers` documentation follows the
README — [Google documentation](https://sphinxcontrib-napoleon.readthedocs.io/en/latest/example_google.html) style for docstrings,
README — although we can write them directly in Markdown.

README — Adding a new model
README — When adding a new model:
README — Create a file `xxx.md` or under `./source/model_doc` (don't hesitate to copy an existing file as template).
README — Link that file in `./source/_toctree.yml`.
README — Write a short overview of the model:
README — Overview with paper & authors
README — Paper abstract
README — Tips and tricks and how to use it best
README — Add the classes that should be linked in the model. This generally includes the configuration, the tokenizer, and
README — every model of that class (the base model, alongside models with additional heads), both in PyTorch and TensorFlow.
README — The order is generally:
README — Tokenizer
README — PyTorch base model
README — PyTorch head models
README — TensorFlow base model
README — TensorFlow head models
README — Flax base model
README — Flax head models
README — These classes should be added using our Markdown syntax. Usually as follows:
README — [!IMPORTANT]
README — Always add a blank line after `[[autodoc]]` to ensure it passes the CI/CD checks.
README — This will include every public method of the configuration that is documented. If for some reason you wish for a method
README — not to be displayed in the documentation, you can do so by specifying which methods should be in the docs:
README — If you just want to add a method that is not documented (for instance magic methods like `__call__` are not documented
README — by default) you can put the list of methods to add in a list that contains `all`:
README — Writing source documentation
README — Values that should be put in `code` should either be surrounded by backticks: \`like so\`. Note that argument names
README — and objects like True, None, or any strings should usually be put in `code`.
README — When mentioning a class, function, or method, it is recommended to use our syntax for internal links so that our tool
README — adds a link to its documentation with this syntax: \[\`XXXClass\`\] or \[\`function\`\]. This requires the class or
README — function to be in the main package.
README — If you want to create a link to some internal class or function, you need to
README — provide its path. For instance: \[\`utils.ModelOutput\`\]. This will be converted into a link with
README — `utils.ModelOutput` in the description. To get rid of the path and only keep the name of the object you are
README — linking to in the description, add a ~: \[\`~utils.ModelOutput\`\] will generate a link with `ModelOutput` in the description.
README — The same works for methods so you can either use \[\`XXXClass.method\`\] or \[\`~XXXClass.method\`\].
README — Defining arguments in a method
README — Arguments should be defined with the `Args:` (or `Arguments:` or `Parameters:`) prefix, followed by a line return and
README — an indentation. The argument should be followed by its type, with its shape if it is a tensor, a colon, and its
README — description:
README — If the description is too long to fit in one line, another indentation is necessary before writing the description
README — after the argument.
README — Here's an example showcasing everything so far:
README — For optional arguments or arguments with defaults we follow the following syntax: imagine we have a function with the
README — following signature:
README — then its documentation should look like this:
README — Note that we always omit the "defaults to \`None\`" when None is the default for any argument. Also note that even
README — if the first line describing your argument type and its default gets long, you can't break it on several lines. You can
README — however, write as many lines as you want in the indented description (see the example above with `input_ids`).

README — Multi-line code blocks can be useful for displaying examples. They are done between two lines of three backticks as usual in Markdown:

README — We follow the [doctest](https://docs.python.org/3/library/doctest.html) syntax for the examples to automatically test
README — the results to stay consistent with the library.

README — The return block should be introduced with the `Returns:` prefix, followed by a line return and an indentation.

README — Adding an image
README — Due to the rapidly growing repository, it is important to make sure that no files that would significantly weigh down the repository are added. This includes images, videos, and other non-text files. We prefer to leverage a hf.co hosted `dataset` like
README — the ones hosted on [`hf-internal-testing`](https://huggingface.co/hf-internal-testing) in which to place these files and reference
README — them by URL. We recommend putting them in the following dataset: [huggingface/documentation-images](https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/documentation-images).
README — If an external contribution, feel free to add the images to your PR and ask a Hugging Face member to migrate your images
README — to this dataset.
README — Styling the docstring
README — We have an automatic script running with the `make style` comment that will make sure that:
README — the docstrings fully take advantage of the line width
README — all code examples are formatted using black, like the code of the Transformers library
README — This script may have some weird failures if you made a syntax mistake or if you uncover a bug. Therefore, it's
README — recommended to commit your changes before running `make style`, so you can revert the changes done by that script
README — Testing documentation examples
README — Good documentation often comes with an example of how a specific function or class should be used.
README — Each model class should contain at least one example showcasing
README — how to use this model class in inference. *E.g.* the class [Wav2Vec2ForCTC](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/model_doc/wav2vec2#transformers.Wav2Vec2ForCTC)
README — includes an example of how to transcribe speech to text in the
README — [docstring of its forward function](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/model_doc/wav2vec2#transformers.Wav2Vec2ForCTC.forward).
README — Writing documentation examples
README — The syntax for Example docstrings can look as follows:
README — The docstring should give a minimal, clear example of how the respective model
README — is to be used in inference and also include the expected (ideally sensible)
README — Often, readers will try out the example before even going through the function
README — or class definitions. Therefore, it is of utmost importance that the example
README — works as expected.
README — Docstring testing
README — To do so each example should be included in the doctests.
README — We use pytests' [doctest integration](https://docs.pytest.org/doctest.html) to verify that all of our examples run correctly.
README — For Transformers, the doctests are run on a daily basis via GitHub Actions as can be
README — seen [here](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/actions/workflows/doctests.yml).

README — Writing doctests
README — Here are a few tips to help you debug the doctests and make them pass:
README — The outputs of the code need to match the expected output **exactly**, so make sure you have the same outputs. In particular doctest will see a difference between single quotes and double quotes, or a missing parenthesis. The only exceptions to that rule are:
README — whitespace: one give whitespace (space, tabulation, new line) is equivalent to any number of whitespace, so you can add new lines where there are spaces to make your output more readable.
README — numerical values: you should never put more than 4 or 5 digits to expected results as different setups or library versions might get you slightly different results. `doctest` is configured to ignore any difference lower than the precision to which you wrote (so 1e-4 if you write 4 digits).
README — Don't leave a block of code that is very long to execute. If you can't make it fast, you can either not use the doctest syntax on it (so that it's ignored), or if you want to use the doctest syntax to show the results, you can add a comment `# doctest: +SKIP` at the end of the lines of code too long to execute
README — Each line of code that produces a result needs to have that result written below. You can ignore an output if you don't want to show it in your code example by adding a comment ` # doctest: +IGNORE_RESULT` at the end of the line of code producing it.

README — Writing metrics to the database
README — `MetricsRecorder` is thread-safe, in the sense of the python [`Thread`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/threading.html#threading.Thread). This means you can start a background thread to do the readings on the device measurements while not blocking the main thread to execute the model measurements.
README — cf [`llama.py`](./llama.py) to see an example of this in practice.

README ja — <h3 align="center">
README ja — <p>JAX、PyTorch、TensorFlowのための最先端機械学習</p>
README ja — <a href="https://hf.co/course"><img src="https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/documentation-images/resolve/main/course_banner.png"></a>
README ja — 🤗Transformersは、テキスト、視覚、音声などの異なるモダリティに対してタスクを実行するために、事前に学習させた数千のモデルを提供します。
README ja — これらのモデルは次のような場合に適用できます:
README ja — 📝 テキストは、テキストの分類、情報抽出、質問応答、要約、翻訳、テキスト生成などのタスクのために、100以上の言語に対応しています。
README ja — 🖼️ 画像分類、物体検出、セグメンテーションなどのタスクのための画像。
README ja — 🗣️ 音声は、音声認識や音声分類などのタスクに使用します。
README ja — トランスフォーマーモデルは、テーブル質問応答、光学文字認識、スキャン文書からの情報抽出、ビデオ分類、視覚的質問応答など、**複数のモダリティを組み合わせた**タスクも実行可能です。
README ja — 🤗Transformersは、与えられたテキストに対してそれらの事前学習されたモデルを素早くダウンロードして使用し、あなた自身のデータセットでそれらを微調整し、私たちの[model hub](https://huggingface.co/models)でコミュニティと共有するためのAPIを提供します。同時に、アーキテクチャを定義する各Pythonモジュールは完全にスタンドアロンであり、迅速な研究実験を可能にするために変更することができます。
README ja — 🤗Transformersは[Jax](https://jax.readthedocs.io/en/latest/)、[PyTorch](https://pytorch.org/)、[TensorFlow](https://www.tensorflow.org/)という3大ディープラーニングライブラリーに支えられ、それぞれのライブラリをシームレスに統合しています。片方でモデルを学習してから、もう片方で推論用にロードするのは簡単なことです。
README ja — [model hub](https://huggingface.co/models)から、ほとんどのモデルのページで直接テストすることができます。また、パブリックモデル、プライベートモデルに対して、[プライベートモデルのホスティング、バージョニング、推論API](https://huggingface.co/pricing)を提供しています。

README ja — トークナイザは学習済みモデルが期待するすべての前処理を担当し、単一の文字列 (上記の例のように) またはリストに対して直接呼び出すことができます。これは下流のコードで使用できる辞書を出力します。また、単純に ** 引数展開演算子を使用してモデルに直接渡すこともできます。
README ja — モデル自体は通常の[Pytorch `nn.Module`](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/nn.html#torch.nn.Module) または [TensorFlow `tf.keras.Model`](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/keras/Model) (バックエンドによって異なる)で、通常通り使用することが可能です。[このチュートリアル](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/training)では、このようなモデルを従来のPyTorchやTensorFlowの学習ループに統合する方法や、私たちの`Trainer`APIを使って新しいデータセットで素早く微調整を行う方法について説明します。

README ja — 使いやすい最新モデル:
README ja — 自然言語理解・生成、コンピュータビジョン、オーディオの各タスクで高いパフォーマンスを発揮します。
README ja — 教育者、実務者にとっての低い参入障壁。
README ja — 学習するクラスは3つだけで、ユーザが直面する抽象化はほとんどありません。
README ja — 学習済みモデルを利用するための統一されたAPI。
README ja — 低い計算コスト、少ないカーボンフットプリント:
README ja — 研究者は、常に再トレーニングを行うのではなく、トレーニングされたモデルを共有することができます。
README ja — 実務家は、計算時間や生産コストを削減することができます。
README ja — すべてのモダリティにおいて、60,000以上の事前学習済みモデルを持つ数多くのアーキテクチャを提供します。
README ja — モデルのライフタイムのあらゆる部分で適切なフレームワークを選択可能:
README ja — 行のコードで最先端のモデルをトレーニング。
README ja — TF2.0/PyTorch/JAXフレームワーク間で1つのモデルを自在に移動させる。
README ja — 学習、評価、生産に適したフレームワークをシームレスに選択できます。
README ja — モデルやサンプルをニーズに合わせて簡単にカスタマイズ可能:
README ja — 原著者が発表した結果を再現するために、各アーキテクチャの例を提供しています。
README ja — モデル内部は可能な限り一貫して公開されています。
README ja — モデルファイルはライブラリとは独立して利用することができ、迅速な実験が可能です。
README ja — なぜtransformersを使ってはいけないのでしょうか？
README ja — このライブラリは、ニューラルネットのためのビルディングブロックのモジュール式ツールボックスではありません。モデルファイルのコードは、研究者が追加の抽象化/ファイルに飛び込むことなく、各モデルを素早く反復できるように、意図的に追加の抽象化でリファクタリングされていません。
README ja — 学習APIはどのようなモデルでも動作するわけではなく、ライブラリが提供するモデルで動作するように最適化されています。一般的な機械学習のループには、別のライブラリ(おそらく[Accelerate](https://huggingface.co/docs/accelerate))を使用する必要があります。
README ja — 私たちはできるだけ多くの使用例を紹介するよう努力していますが、[examples フォルダ](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/tree/main/examples) にあるスクリプトはあくまで例です。あなたの特定の問題に対してすぐに動作するわけではなく、あなたのニーズに合わせるために数行のコードを変更する必要があることが予想されます。
README ja — このリポジトリは、Python 3.9+, Flax 0.4.1+, PyTorch 2.1+, TensorFlow 2.6+ でテストされています。
README ja — 🤗Transformersは[仮想環境](https://docs.python.org/3/library/venv.html)にインストールする必要があります。Pythonの仮想環境に慣れていない場合は、[ユーザーガイド](https://packaging.python.org/guides/installing-using-pip-and-virtual-environments/)を確認してください。
README ja — まず、使用するバージョンのPythonで仮想環境を作成し、アクティベートします。
README ja — その後、Flax, PyTorch, TensorFlowのうち少なくとも1つをインストールする必要があります。
README ja — [TensorFlowインストールページ](https://www.tensorflow.org/install/)、[PyTorchインストールページ](https://pytorch.org/get-started/locally/#start-locally)、[Flax](https://github.com/google/flax#quick-install)、[Jax](https://github.com/google/jax#installation)インストールページで、お使いのプラットフォーム別のインストールコマンドを参照してください。

README ja — もしサンプルを試したい、またはコードの最先端が必要で、新しいリリースを待てない場合は、[ライブラリをソースからインストール](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/installation#installing-from-source)する必要があります。

README zh-hant — <h3 align="center">
README zh-hant — <p>為 Jax、PyTorch 以及 TensorFlow 打造的先進自然語言處理函式庫</p>
README zh-hant — <a href="https://hf.co/course"><img src="https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/documentation-images/resolve/main/course_banner.png"></a>
README zh-hant — 🤗 Transformers 提供了數以千計的預訓練模型，支援 100 多種語言的文本分類、資訊擷取、問答、摘要、翻譯、文本生成。它的宗旨是讓最先進的 NLP 技術人人易用。
README zh-hant — 🤗 Transformers 提供了便於快速下載和使用的API，讓你可以將預訓練模型用在給定文本、在你的資料集上微調然後經由 [model hub](https://huggingface.co/models) 與社群共享。同時，每個定義的 Python 模組架構均完全獨立，方便修改和快速研究實驗。
README zh-hant — 🤗 Transformers 支援三個最熱門的深度學習函式庫： [Jax](https://jax.readthedocs.io/en/latest/), [PyTorch](https://pytorch.org/) 以及 [TensorFlow](https://www.tensorflow.org/) — 並與之完美整合。你可以直接使用其中一個框架訓練你的模型，然後用另一個載入和推論。
README zh-hant — 你可以直接在 [model hub](https://huggingface.co/models) 上測試大多數的模型。我們也提供了 [私有模型託管、模型版本管理以及推論API](https://huggingface.co/pricing)。
README zh-hant — 這裡是一些範例：
README zh-hant — [用 BERT 做遮蓋填詞](https://huggingface.co/google-bert/bert-base-uncased?text=Paris+is+the+%5BMASK%5D+of+France)
README zh-hant — [用 Electra 做專有名詞辨識](https://huggingface.co/dbmdz/electra-large-discriminator-finetuned-conll03-english?text=My+name+is+Sarah+and+I+live+in+London+city)
README zh-hant — [用 GPT-2 做文本生成](https://huggingface.co/openai-community/gpt2?text=A+long+time+ago%2C+)
README zh-hant — [用 RoBERTa 做自然語言推論](https://huggingface.co/FacebookAI/roberta-large-mnli?text=The+dog+was+lost.+Nobody+lost+any+animal)
README zh-hant — [用 BART 做文本摘要](https://huggingface.co/facebook/bart-large-cnn?text=The+tower+is+324+metres+%281%2C063+ft%29+tall%2C+about+the+same+height+as+an+81-storey+building%2C+and+the+tallest+structure+in+Paris.+Its+base+is+square%2C+measuring+125+metres+%28410+ft%29+on+each+side.+During+its+construction%2C+the+Eiffel+Tower+surpassed+the+Washington+Monument+to+become+the+tallest+man-made+structure+in+the+world%2C+a+title+it+held+for+41+years+until+the+Chrysler+Building+in+New+York+City+was+finished+in+1930.+It+was+the+first+structure+to+reach+a+height+of+300+metres.+Due+to+the+addition+of+a+broadcasting+aerial+at+the+top+of+the+tower+in+1957%2C+it+is+now+taller+than+the+Chrysler+Building+by+5.2+metres+%2817+ft%29.+Excluding+transmitters%2C+the+Eiffel+Tower+is+the+second+tallest+free-standing+structure+in+France+after+the+Millau+Viaduct)
README zh-hant — [用 DistilBERT 做問答](https://huggingface.co/distilbert/distilbert-base-uncased-distilled-squad?text=Which+name+is+also+used+to+describe+the+Amazon+rainforest+in+English%3F&context=The+Amazon+rainforest+%28Portuguese%3A+Floresta+Amaz%C3%B4nica+or+Amaz%C3%B4nia%3B+Spanish%3A+Selva+Amaz%C3%B3nica%2C+Amazon%C3%ADa+or+usually+Amazonia%3B+French%3A+For%C3%AAt+amazonienne%3B+Dutch%3A+Amazoneregenwoud%29%2C+also+known+in+English+as+Amazonia+or+the+Amazon+Jungle%2C+is+a+moist+broadleaf+forest+that+covers+most+of+the+Amazon+basin+of+South+America.+This+basin+encompasses+7%2C000%2C000+square+kilometres+%282%2C700%2C000+sq+mi%29%2C+of+which+5%2C500%2C000+square+kilometres+%282%2C100%2C000+sq+mi%29+are+covered+by+the+rainforest.+This+region+includes+territory+belonging+to+nine+nations.+The+majority+of+the+forest+is+contained+within+Brazil%2C+with+60%25+of+the+rainforest%2C+followed+by+Peru+with+13%25%2C+Colombia+with+10%25%2C+and+with+minor+amounts+in+Venezuela%2C+Ecuador%2C+Bolivia%2C+Guyana%2C+Suriname+and+French+Guiana.+States+or+departments+in+four+nations+contain+%22Amazonas%22+in+their+names.+The+Amazon+represents+over+half+of+the+planet%27s+remaining+rainforests%2C+and+comprises+the+largest+and+most+biodiverse+tract+of+tropical+rainforest+in+the+world%2C+with+an+estimated+390+billion+individual+trees+divided+into+16%2C000+species)
README zh-hant — [用 T5 做翻譯](https://huggingface.co/google-t5/t5-base?text=My+name+is+Wolfgang+and+I+live+in+Berlin)
README zh-hant — [Write With Transformer](https://transformer.huggingface.co)**，由 Hugging Face 團隊所打造，是一個文本生成的官方 demo。
README zh-hant — 如果你在尋找由 Hugging Face 團隊所提供的客製化支援服務
README zh-hant — <a target="_blank" href="https://huggingface.co/support">

README zh-hant — 第二行程式碼下載並快取 pipeline 使用的預訓練模型，而第三行程式碼則在給定的文本上進行了評估。這裡的答案“正面” (positive) 具有 99.97% 的信賴度。
README zh-hant — 許多的 NLP 任務都有隨選即用的預訓練 `pipeline`。例如，我們可以輕鬆地從給定文本中擷取問題答案：
README zh-hant — 除了提供問題解答，預訓練模型還提供了對應的信賴度分數以及解答在 tokenized 後的文本中開始和結束的位置。你可以從[這個教學](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/task_summary)了解更多 `pipeline` API支援的任務。
README zh-hant — 要在你的任務中下載和使用任何預訓練模型很簡單，只需三行程式碼。這裡是 PyTorch 版的範例：
README zh-hant — 這裡是對應的 TensorFlow 程式碼：
README zh-hant — Tokenizer 為所有的預訓練模型提供了預處理，並可以直接轉換單一字串（比如上面的例子）或串列 (list)。它會輸出一個的字典 (dict) 讓你可以在下游程式碼裡使用或直接藉由 `**` 運算式傳給模型。
README zh-hant — 模型本身是一個常規的 [Pytorch `nn.Module`](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/nn.html#torch.nn.Module) 或 [TensorFlow `tf.keras.Model`](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/keras/Model)（取決於你的後端），可依常規方式使用。 [這個教學](https://huggingface.co/transformers/training.html)解釋了如何將這樣的模型整合到一般的 PyTorch 或 TensorFlow 訓練迴圈中，或是如何使用我們的 `Trainer` API 在一個新的資料集上快速進行微調。
README zh-hant — 為什麼要用 transformers？
README zh-hant — 便於使用的先進模型：
README zh-hant — NLU 和 NLG 上性能卓越
README zh-hant — 對教學和實作友好且低門檻
README zh-hant — 高度抽象，使用者只須學習 3 個類別
README zh-hant — 對所有模型使用的制式化API
README zh-hant — 更低的運算成本，更少的碳排放：
README zh-hant — 研究人員可以分享已訓練的模型而非每次從頭開始訓練
README zh-hant — 工程師可以減少計算時間以及生產成本
README zh-hant — 數十種模型架構、兩千多個預訓練模型、100多種語言支援
README zh-hant — 對於模型生命週期的每一個部分都面面俱到：
README zh-hant — 訓練先進的模型，只需 3 行程式碼
README zh-hant — 模型可以在不同深度學習框架之間任意轉換
README zh-hant — 為訓練、評估和生產選擇最適合的框架，並完美銜接
README zh-hant — 為你的需求輕鬆客製化專屬模型和範例：
README zh-hant — 我們為每種模型架構提供了多個範例來重現原論文結果
README zh-hant — 一致的模型內部架構
README zh-hant — 模型檔案可單獨使用，便於修改和快速實驗
README zh-hant — 什麼情況下我不該用 transformers？
README zh-hant — 本函式庫並不是模組化的神經網絡工具箱。模型文件中的程式碼並未做額外的抽象封裝，以便研究人員快速地翻閱及修改程式碼，而不會深陷複雜的類別包裝之中。
README zh-hant — `Trainer` API 並非相容任何模型，它只為本函式庫中的模型最佳化。對於一般的機器學習用途，請使用其他函式庫。
README zh-hant — 儘管我們已盡力而為，[examples 目錄](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/tree/main/examples)中的腳本也僅為範例而已。對於特定問題，它們並不一定隨選即用，可能需要修改幾行程式碼以符合需求。
README zh-hant — 這個 Repository 已在 Python 3.9+、Flax 0.4.1+、PyTorch 2.1+ 和 TensorFlow 2.6+ 下經過測試。
README zh-hant — 你可以在[虛擬環境](https://docs.python.org/3/library/venv.html)中安裝 🤗 Transformers。如果你還不熟悉 Python 的虛擬環境，請閱此[使用者指引](https://packaging.python.org/guides/installing-using-pip-and-virtual-environments/)。
README zh-hant — 首先，用你打算使用的版本的 Python 創建一個虛擬環境並進入。
README zh-hant — 然後，你需要安裝 Flax、PyTorch 或 TensorFlow 其中之一。對於該如何在你使用的平台上安裝這些框架，請參閱 [TensorFlow 安裝頁面](https://www.tensorflow.org/install/), [PyTorch 安裝頁面](https://pytorch.org/get-started/locally/#start-locally) 或 [Flax 安裝頁面](https://github.com/google/flax#quick-install)。
README zh-hant — 當其中一個後端安裝成功後，🤗 Transformers 可依此安裝：
README zh-hant — 如果你想要試試範例或者想在正式發布前使用最新開發中的程式碼，你必須[從原始碼安裝](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/installation#installing-from-source)。
README zh-hant — 使用 conda
README zh-hant — 🤗 Transformers 可以藉由 conda 依此安裝：
README zh-hant — _筆記:_** 從 `huggingface` 頻道安裝 `transformers` 已被淘汰。
README zh-hant — 要藉由 conda 安裝 Flax、PyTorch 或 TensorFlow 其中之一，請參閱它們各自安裝頁面的說明。
README zh-hant — 🤗 Transformers 支援的[所有的模型檢查點](https://huggingface.co/models)**，由[使用者](https://huggingface.co/users)和[組織](https://huggingface.co/organizations)上傳，均與 huggingface.co [model hub](https://huggingface.co) 完美結合。
README zh-hant — 目前的檢查點數量： ![](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://huggingface.co/api/shields/models&color=brightgreen)
README zh-hant — 🤗 Transformers 目前支援以下的架構: 模型概覽請參閱[這裡](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/model_summary).
README zh-hant — 要檢查某個模型是否已有 Flax、PyTorch 或 TensorFlow 的實作，或其是否在🤗 Tokenizers 函式庫中有對應的 tokenizer，敬請參閱[此表](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/index#supported-frameworks)。
README zh-hant — 這些實作均已於多個資料集測試（請參閱範例腳本）並應與原版實作表現相當。你可以在範例文件的[此節](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/examples)中了解實作的細節。
README zh-hant — | 章節 | 描述 |

README zh-hant — | [快速上手：微調和範例腳本](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/tree/main/examples) | 為各種任務提供的範例腳本 |

README ur — <p>جدید ترین مشین لرننگ برائے JAX، PyTorch اور TensorFlow</p>
README ur — <a href="https://hf.co/course"><img src="https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/documentation-images/resolve/main/course_banner.png"></a>
README ur — &#8207;🤗 Transformers مختلف طریقوں جیسے کہ متن، بصارت، اور آڈیو پر کام کرنے کے لیے ہزاروں پری ٹرینڈ ماڈلز فراہم کرتے ہیں۔
README ur — یہ ماڈلز درج ذیل پر لاگو کیے جا سکتے ہیں:
README ur — 📝 متن، جیسے کہ متن کی درجہ بندی، معلومات کا استخراج، سوالات کے جوابات، خلاصہ، ترجمہ، اور متن کی تخلیق، 100 سے زائد زبانوں میں۔
README ur — 🖼️ تصاویر، جیسے کہ تصویر کی درجہ بندی، اشیاء کی شناخت، اور تقسیم۔
README ur — 🗣️ آڈیو، جیسے کہ تقریر کی شناخت اور آڈیو کی درجہ بندی۔
README ur — ٹرانسفارمر ماڈلز **مختلف طریقوں کو ملا کر** بھی کام انجام دے سکتے ہیں، جیسے کہ ٹیبل سوال جواب، بصری حروف کی شناخت، اسکین شدہ دستاویزات سے معلومات نکالنا، ویڈیو کی درجہ بندی، اور بصری سوال جواب۔
README ur — &#8207;🤗 Transformers ایسے APIs فراہم کرتا ہے جو آپ کو تیز رفتاری سے پری ٹرینڈ ماڈلز کو ایک دیے گئے متن پر ڈاؤن لوڈ اور استعمال کرنے، انہیں اپنے ڈیٹا سیٹس پر فائن ٹون کرنے، اور پھر ہمارے [ماڈل حب](https://huggingface.co/models) پر کمیونٹی کے ساتھ شیئر کرنے کی سہولت دیتا ہے۔ اسی وقت، ہر پائتھن ماڈیول جو ایک آرکیٹیکچر کو بیان کرتا ہے، مکمل طور پر خود مختار ہوتا ہے اور اسے تیز تحقیقاتی تجربات کے لیے تبدیل کیا جا سکتا ہے۔
README ur — &#8207;🤗 Transformers تین سب سے مشہور ڈیپ لرننگ لائبریریوں — [Jax](https://jax.readthedocs.io/en/latest/)، [PyTorch](https://pytorch.org/) اور [TensorFlow](https://www.tensorflow.org/) — کی مدد سے تیار کردہ ہے، جن کے درمیان بے حد ہموار انضمام ہے۔ اپنے ماڈلز کو ایک کے ساتھ تربیت دینا اور پھر دوسرے کے ساتھ inference کے لیے لوڈ کرنا انتہائی سادہ ہے۔

README ur — آپ ہمارے زیادہ تر ماڈلز کو براہ راست ان کے صفحات پر [ماڈل ہب](https://huggingface.co/models) سے آزما سکتے ہیں۔ ہم عوامی اور نجی ماڈلز کے لیے [ذاتی ماڈل ہوسٹنگ، ورژننگ، اور انفرنس API](https://huggingface.co/pricing) بھی فراہم کرتے ہیں۔
